bibliographic.title: Action valuation of on- and off-ball soccer players based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning

scope.rationale: Proposes a valuation method for on- and off-ball soccer players in a single holistic framework based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning, estimating Q-values per player per action including off-ball movement directions.

model.name: Multi-agent deep RL with action supervision (on- and off-ball valuation)
inputs: 2D position and velocity of the ball (23 x 2 x 2 dimensions, 92-dim state)
one-hot action vector for each agent (14 actions)
event labels (passing, shooting) from event data
model.target: Q-value (state-action value) of each of 14 actions for each of 10 attacking players at each frame, trained via SARSA TD-loss with terminal rewards (Goal: +1, EPV at terminal no-goal, Conceding: -1)
model.architecture: Recurrent neural network with single 64-dim GRU middle layer (ReLU), input 106 x 64 (state 92-dim + action 14-dim), output 64 x 14 Q-values; trained with SARSA TD loss + cross-entropy action-supervision loss (L_AS) + L1 regularization; Adam optimizer; lambda_1 = 0.01, lambda_2 = 0.1
model.temporal_horizon: until end of possession (attack sequence; min 50 frames, max T=300 frames equivalent to 30 seconds at 10 Hz)

data.provider: Data Stadium Inc. (event + tracking); J.League (season goals); Soccer-digest (expert ratings)

baselines: C-OBSO (Creating off-ball scoring opportunity) [Teranishi et al. 2022]
evaluation.splits: Match/team-level: training and validation data = attack sequences from teams other than Yokohama F. Marinos (1669 train + 186 val); test data = Yokohama F. Marinos attack sequences (1236 series). Player valuation restricted to attacks within the attacking third.

claims.statement: TD loss with action supervision (0.0034 +/- 0.0001) was smaller than that without supervision (0.0063 +/- 0.0004), while L_AS with supervision (3.9550 +/- 0.0005) was slightly larger than without supervision (3.9407 +/- 0.0005).

Average on-ball Q-values with supervision (0.0137 +/- 2.597 x 10^-4) were larger than those without supervision (0.0008 +/- 4.431 x 10^-5); average off-ball Q-values with supervision (0.0008 +/- 0.0035) were also larger than those without supervision (-7.123 +/- 0.0018).

There was a high negative correlation (rho = -0.761) between season goals and average Q-values obtained by the proposed method, indicating the indicator tends to value defensive players who provided many passes.
There was a moderate positive correlation between average on-ball and off-ball Q-values (rho = 0.618), suggesting the indicator tends to value similar play style between on- and off-ball situations.
Low negative correlation between average rating by experts and average Q-value (rho = -0.218).
Low negative correlation with average OBSO (rho = -0.305).
No significant correlation with average C-OBSO (rho = 0.182, p > 0.05).

The proposed method values on- and off-ball actions of multiple players (including those far from the ball) in a single holistic framework using multi-agent deep RL with discrete action space (14 actions) over continuous state space inspired by Google Research Football.
Off-ball players spend approximately 87 min of 90 min without the ball, motivating evaluation of off-ball contribution.

limitations: Since there is no true value for the Q-value, the performance of the model cannot be directly validated; only relationships with existing indicators were investigated.

Action supervision requires careful interpretation: too little supervision (lambda_1 << 0.01) yields insufficient learning of counterfactual action values, while too much (lambda_1 >> 0.01) may overfit to actual actions and not consider counterfactual actions.
Sample size for correlation analysis was small (N = 14 players who played at least 10 games), so rho was used as an effect size rather than p-values.
Tracking data for all players and timesteps in the J1 League are not publicly shared in such amounts, limiting reproducibility.
Goalkeeper was excluded; only 10 attacking-player RL agent models were constructed.
Player valuation was restricted to attacks within the attacking third for simplicity.
The model can only qualitatively investigate effectiveness in terms of modeling soccer agents, not quantitatively validate which model is best in a practical sense.
open_questions: Improve RL models for a more valid valuation of players.
Use more sophisticated rewards per action.

critic.notes: Initial batch extraction; critic pending. Unique multi-agent RL handling on+off ball jointly.
